pages.title: The Listener Becomes the Phantom
body: Question: Who is The Phantom: a character we tell stories about, or a state of mind the listener becomes?
Discovery: The Locksmith is not about breaking in. It is about becoming someone who can build anything.
Decision: Every track will represent a stage in the transformation from ordinary to extraordinary.
THIS CHANGED EVERYTHING
• Track titles
• Track purposes
• The emotional arc
• The album artwork concept
• How we talk about the album
Why it matters: When someone presses play, they do not just listen. They step into a different identity.

"We're not macking music for hackers.
We're making music for builders." - AG

pages.title: Why the Notebook Exists
body: Question: How do we show the thinking that led to the commits, not merely the commits themselves?
Discovery: The notebook is not a recap. It is the place where motives, dead ends, and decisions remain visible.
Decision: Publish entries from the same semantic document source used by the authoring workspace.
Why it matters: Artifacts feel more human when the reader can see the path that shaped them.

body.text: A note on preserving the thinking behind the finished artifact.

pages.title: The Four-Page Notebook Test
body:
This entry exists to test the full multi-page publishing loop.

For the first time, a single Scriptorium note should be able to move beyond the original two-page notebook view. The Admin can now assign content to Page 1, Page 2, Page 3, and Page 4, and the hidden Live Notebook should let a visitor turn through those pages under one slug.

The important thing is not just that more content can be stored. The important thing is that the authored structure survives the journey from Admin to export to the public notebook.
Question: Can one Scriptorium entry behave like a real notebook entry with multiple pages, while still publishing as one clean, shareable slug?
What this test should confirm
• The entry opens at Page 1.
• The first visible view shows Pages 1-2.
• The next page control reveals Pages 3-4.
• The entry keeps one slug.
• Page-specific content does not collapse back into Page 1.
• Legacy two-page entries still work.
• Visitor-facing language says pages, not spreads.
Discovery: The page model is now based on page numbers instead of only left and right sides. That means the author can think in simple terms: Page 1, Page 2, Page 3, Page 4.

This is the first page beyond the original two-page limit.

If this text appears only after turning the page, the Live Notebook is correctly reading the nested pages array instead of relying only on the legacy spread fields.
Breakthrough: The notebook is no longer limited to a single visible pair of pages. One entry can now become a longer authored artifact without being split into separate posts.

Decision: The multi-page Live Notebook feature should be considered ready when this entry publishes under one slug, opens at Page 1, turns cleanly to Pages 3-4, and preserves the Page 3 visual decoration without breaking older entries.
Final verification steps
1. Publish this entry from Scriptorium Admin.
2. Open the hidden Live Notebook page.
3. Confirm the entry starts on Pages 1-2.
4. Use Next page to turn to Pages 3-4.
5. Confirm the Page 3 visual element appears on Page 3.
6. Confirm Previous page returns to Pages 1-2.
7. Confirm the entry browser and entry navigation still work.

Why it matters: This turns Scriptorium from a beautiful two-page presentation into a real notebook publishing system. Longer thoughts, build records, reflections, and visual process notes can now stay together as one complete entry.

If this text appears only after turning the page, the Live Notebook is correctly reading the nested pages array instead of relying only on the legacy spread fields.

body.label: Breakthrough
body.text: The notebook is no longer limited to a single visible pair of pages. One entry can now become a longer authored artifact without being split into separate posts.

body.label: Decision
body.text: The multi-page Live Notebook feature should be considered ready when this entry publishes under one slug, opens at Page 1, turns cleanly to Pages 3-4, and preserves the Page 3 visual decoration without breaking older entries.

body.title: Final verification steps
items: Publish this entry from Scriptorium Admin.
Open the hidden Live Notebook page.
Confirm the entry starts on Pages 1-2.
Use Next page to turn to Pages 3-4.
Confirm the Page 3 visual element appears on Page 3.
Confirm Previous page returns to Pages 1-2.
Confirm the entry browser and entry navigation still work.

body.label: Why it matters
body.text: This turns Scriptorium from a beautiful two-page presentation into a real notebook publishing system. Longer thoughts, build records, reflections, and visual process notes can now stay together as one complete entry.

This entry exists to test the full multi-page publishing loop.

For the first time, a single Scriptorium note should be able to move beyond the original two-page notebook view. The Admin can now assign content to Page 1, Page 2, Page 3, and Page 4, and the hidden Live Notebook should let a visitor turn through those pages under one slug.

The important thing is not just that more content can be stored. The important thing is that the authored structure survives the journey from Admin to export to the public notebook.
